1.8K views · 229 reactions | Americans feel worse about the economy right now than they did during the 2008 financial crisis, COVID, or 9/11.

The University of Michigan’s preliminary consumer sentiment index fell to 46.3 in October 2026, down from 48.1 in September. If it holds in the final reading on Oct 23, it’ll be the second-lowest level in the survey’s 74-year history, below the Great Recession (November 2008 came in at 55.3), the pandemic, 9/11, the 1970s oil crisis, and the Vietnam War. Americans’ view of current economic conditions fell 12% in a month to 44.7, an all-time low. The steepest declines came from lower-income households and people with little exposure to the stock market.

That’s the K-shaped economy in one survey. People with investments are riding the market. People living on a paycheck are absorbing higher prices, rates, and costs, without a crash or a headline to point to. Nothing broke. It just keeps costing more.

Source: University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers, preliminary October 2026 (via CNN and Bloomberg, Oct 9, 2026).
